title: Global Accelerator, Local Zones & Wavelength
summary: Improve global TCP/UDP performance with anycast IPs, and push compute closer to users.
tldr: **Global Accelerator** gives you **static anycast IP addresses**. Users enter the AWS network at the nearest edge location and ride the backbone to healthy ALB, NLB, EC2 or Elastic IP endpoints in one or more Regions.
Pick it for **non-HTTP (UDP/TCP) traffic**, **fixed IPs to allowlist or hard-code**, and **regional failover in seconds without DNS caching**. It doesn't cache; that's CloudFront.
To move the *compute* closer: **Local Zones** (metro areas), **Wavelength** (inside a carrier's 5G network), **Outposts** (your own building).

keyFacts.text: An accelerator gets two static anycast IPv4 addresses (four with dual-stack: two IPv4, two IPv6). They stay assigned until you delete the accelerator, while endpoints change behind them.
Each endpoint group has a **traffic dial** (0–100%) to shift traffic between Regions gradually, for example to drain a Region during maintenance.
A **custom routing accelerator** maps an accelerator port deterministically to one EC2 instance IP and port in a VPC subnet, for matchmaking-style game sessions.
Failover happens inside the AWS network based on health checks, so clients don't wait for DNS caches to expire as with Route 53 failover.
Local Zones and Wavelength Zones run EC2, EBS and other services as extensions of a parent Region's VPC, using the same APIs and tools.

traps: CloudFront doesn't proxy arbitrary UDP protocols; game traffic over UDP points to Global Accelerator.
Route 53 failover with a low TTL still depends on resolvers and clients honoring the TTL; it isn't "within seconds without DNS caching".
Moving Elastic IPs between Regions is impossible; EIPs are Regional.
A standard accelerator load-balances to healthy endpoints; it can't pin a player to a specific instance port. That needs custom routing.
A custom routing accelerator runs no health checks and never fails over, because you choose the destination; use a standard accelerator when Regional failover is the goal.
Wavelength is for mobile 5G clients; a studio on a wired office network wants a Local Zone.
